title: Officers cleared by police watchdog in 2016 Remand Centre death of inmate
article: After a nearly two-year long investigation into the October 2016 death of a man at the Winnipeg Remand Centre, the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) has announced no police officers will face any charges.

In a media release on Friday, the IIU said the incident that was under investigation began when a man was arrested at a convenience store on Ellice Avenue on Oct. 11, 2016. IIU said officers of the Winnipeg Police Service (WPS) transported the man to the Winnipeg Remand Centre and early the next morning a struggle between the man, three corrections officers and two members of the WPS took place in a shower room. IIU said during the struggle the man suffered a medical emergency and became unresponsive at which time he was taken to the Health Sciences Centre where he was pronounced dead.

IIU said due to the fact that the man's death could have been caused by a police officer, they were mandated to investigate the incident, a process that included interviews with police and corrections officers, and reviewing audio and video recordings from the Remand Centre. In addition the IIU received a pathology report which determined the man died from cardiac arrhythmia which was made worse by the methamphetamine in his bloodstream and the stress and injuries from the struggle.

The IIU investigation forwarded the complete investigation file to Manitoba Prosecution Services, requesting that it review the file. As a result, Manitoba Prosecution Services advised IIU there is no reasonable likelihood of either police officer being convicted. Based on this advice, neither officer will face any Criminal Code charges arising from this matter. On Friday, the IIU announced their investigation was officially closed.
"There is no normal, every investigation is different," said Barbara Czech, communications spokesperson for the IIU. "The investigation goes where the investigation goes."
An inquest into the man's death will take place as required by the Fatality Inquiries Act.
